description: Create a new Postmortem Status in OneUptime. Returns the created Postmortem Status object with its ID. Use this to add new Postmortem Statuses to your project. Note: projectId is inferred from your API key — you do not need to provide it.

color.description: Color of this resource in Hex (#32a852 for example).

description.description: Friendly description that will help you remember.
description.example: This is an example of longer text content that might be stored in this field.

isArchived.description: Archived statuses stay on the incidents whose postmortems are in them, but can't be picked again. The not started, draft and completed statuses can't be archived.

isCompletedStatus.description: Is it the status a postmortem moves to once it is published on a status page? A postmortem in this status, or in one below it, counts as done. A project has one, and it can't be deleted or archived.

isDraftStatus.description: Is it the status a postmortem moves to once its note is written? A project has one, and it can't be deleted or archived.

isNotStartedStatus.description: Is it the status a new incident's postmortem starts in? A project has one, and it can't be deleted or archived.

name.description: Any friendly name of this object.

order.description: Where this status sits in the project's list of postmortem statuses: 1 is the top. A postmortem in the completed status, or in a status below it, counts as done; one above it is still owed. So the not started, draft and completed statuses have to stay in that order. A new status without a number goes just above the completed status. Setting a number moves the status to that place, and the ones in between shift by one. In the dashboard, drag the rows to reorder them.

projectId.description: ID of your OneUptime Project in which this object belongs.
